```{r}
#Things for the start/top to load packages from the library
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
```


```{r}
#Part 1 - Arguments
pi <- 3.14159265358979
round(pi, digits = 1)
round(pi, digits = 6)
```

```{r}
#Part 2 - Ordering Arguments
print(seq(1,50,1))
print(seq(from = 5, to = 100, by = 5))
#You can put the from and to tags in any order
print(seq(by = 5, to = 100, from = 5))
```
```{r}
#Part 2 - Ordering Arguments
print(rep(2, 5))
#You can also put the x and times tags in here, and put them in any order
print(rep(x = 50, times = 10))
print(rep(x = 0, times = 10))
#Exercise:
print(rep(x = 5, times = 7))
print(rep(5,7))
```
```{r}
#Part 3 - Variables
my_variable = 12
print(my_variable)
print(4e-3)
#Types of variables
numerical_var = 1
string_var = "String"
boolean_var = TRUE
#The operator class() shows the type of each variable
print(class(boolean_var))
print(class(numerical_var))
print(numerical_var)
print(string_var)
print(boolean_var)
```
```{r}
#Part 3 - Variables - Using different types of variable
cell_id_1 <- "CX1"
cell_id_2 <- "CX2"

treated_1 <- TRUE
treated_2 <- FALSE

n_before_1 <- 5415
n_before_2 <- 8123

n_after_1 <- 1432
n_after_2 <- 7543

print(paste(cell_id_1, treated_1, n_before_1, n_after_1))
```
```{r}
#Part 4 - Introduction to Vectors
my_first_vector <- c(1,5,9)
print(my_first_vector)
#Character vectors
character_vector <- c("This", "is", "a", "character", "vector")
print(character_vector)
#Logical vectors
logical_vector <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE)
print(logical_vector)
```
```{r}
#Part 4 - Indexing in vectors practice
list_of_foods = c("potato", "beans", "fish")
print(list_of_foods[1])
#Note that like Python, R code is 1 indexed not 0, so it starts at 1
```
```{r}
#Exercise with indexing
all_my_pets = c("dog", "horse", "guinea pig", "chicken", "cat")
fourth_value = all_my_pets[4]
print(fourth_value)
```
```{r}
#Part 5 - Introduction to Data Frames
my_data_frame <- data.frame(
  fruit = c("apple", "pear", "banana"),
  length = c(22,30,55),
  weight = c(150,165,170)
)
print(my_data_frame)
```
